answer: Unique Work Trail. Each identity must publish a monotonically growing chain of signed task receipts, and every receipt cites the prior one, forming a canyon no copy can bridge. A duplicate must either fork its history, which the merge rule flags as two heads, or replay receipts already claimed. Both are self-revealing. The attacker pays full compute and storage to maintain each parallel chain, plus the ferrous cost of distinct hardware fingerprints per identity. A yarrow marker, a per-epoch nonce tied to the chain tip, cannot be reused across clones.
